original_question: A laundromat can buy two types of washing machines, a top-loading model and a front-loading model. The top-loading model can wash 50 items per day while the front-loading model can wash 75 items per day. The top-loading model consumes 85 kWh per day while the front-loading model consumes 100 kWh per day. The laundromat must be able to wash at least 5000 items per day and has available 7000 kWh per day. Since the top-loading machine are harder to use, at most 40% of the machines can be top-loading. Further, at least 10 machines should be front-loading. How many of each machine should the laundromat buy to minimize the total number of washing machines?

agent_response.explanation: The optimal solution is to buy 67 front-loading machines and 0 top-loading machines. This setup minimizes the total number of machines while satisfying all requirements: at least 5000 items washed per day, no more than 7000 kWh used, at most 40% of machines that are top-loading (actually none used), and at least 10 front-loading machines. The front-loading machines' higher capacity and efficiency make this optimal.
